as_written_in_papers.quote: This revealed a heterozygous de novo LAMP2 frameshift mutation (c.406dupA, p.T136NfsTer3), absent in population databases and parental testing, confirming Danon disease (see Supplementary material online, Figure S1).

cases.statement: One person: a 36-year-old heterozygous woman with ventricular fibrillation, dilated hypertrabeculated left ventricle without hypertrophy; died of sudden cardiac arrest 6 months later.

people.label: patient (A 36-year-old woman)
people.key_phenotypes: ventricular fibrillation resuscitated; first-degree AV block and intraventricular conduction delay; dilated left ventricle (EF 37-40%) with hypertrabeculation and normal wall thickness; transmural/mid-wall late gadolinium enhancement; non-sustained ventricular tachycardia; sudden cardiac death 6 months later

quotes.quote: Shortly after arrival, she developed ventricular fibrillation and was successfully resuscitated.

Electrocardiography demonstrated sinus rhythm with first-degree atrioventricular block (PR interval 216 ms) and mildly prolonged QRS duration (125 ms) consistent with intraventricular conduction delay (Figure 1A).
Transthoracic echocardiography (Figure 1B and C) revealed a left ventricular ejection fraction of 40%, wall thickness within normal limits, and apical hypertrabeculation.

Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (Figure 1E and F) demonstrated a dilated left ventricle (end-diastolic volume 212 mL, EF 37%), trabeculation ratio of 2.5 in the lateral wall, and transmural late gadolinium enhancement in the apical and distal lateral segments, with T1/T2 mapping consistent with fibrosis.
She died from sudden cardiac arrest 6 months later.

phenotype_specificity.statement: Authors describe the phenotype (dilated, fibrotic, hypertrabeculated, no hypertrophy) as atypical for Danon disease. Negative family history stated. Other genes tested or excluded not reported; testing method not stated in the text.

quotes.quote: The phenotype was dilated, fibrotic, and hypertrabeculated—distinct from classical hypertrophy.
There was no family history of cardiomyopathy, sudden death, or neuromuscular disease.

de_novo.statement: Authors state the variant was absent on parental testing and call it de novo; whether both parents were tested is implied by 'parental testing' but not stated explicitly; parentage confirmation not reported.

quotes.quote: This revealed a heterozygous de novo LAMP2 frameshift mutation (c.406dupA, p.T136NfsTer3), absent in population databases and parental testing, confirming Danon disease (see Supplementary material online, Figure S1).

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: From the batch HGVS, c.406dup is a one-base duplication causing a frameshift, predicted p.(Thr136AsnfsTer3). The paper states no mechanism beyond 'frameshift'.

population_data_in_papers.statement: Authors state the variant is absent from population databases (databases not named).

concerns: Parental testing is summarised in one phrase; individual parental results and parentage confirmation are not given in the text (Supplementary Figure S1 not available here).
